messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> PAGER:PD-8421 (region: west2, symptom: CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED / GPU memory pressure)

pagerduty-app: Incident created: PD-8421 assigned to oncall (anya) · https://pd.example/pd/PD-8421

anya: acked. I'm on it, starting initial triage.

sam: I'm online, ping me if you need pool-level ops.

anya: Quick check — dashboards show a spike in OOMs across pool gpu-west2a, ~12 distinct alloc failures in last 90s. Latency bump on inference-route: /v1/generate (p50->p95).

mikhail: Logs show recurring: `cudaRuntimeGetLastError: out of memory` from runtime-infer pod. snippet:```
[2026-03-17T18:05:21Z] runtime-infer-23 cuda:172 alloc failed size=1.2GB
[2026-03-17T18:05:21Z] evict: kvcache reclaim insufficient
```

anya: Running `kubectl` to identify affected pods
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-west2a
# runtime-infer-23   1/2 OOMKilled   10.12.4.23
# runtime-infer-41   1/2 OOMKilled   10.12.4.29
```

sam: I'm going to drain the smallest-remaining pods in that pool to reduce pressure. Command I'll run: `infractl pool drain --pool gpu-west2a --selector shard=serve --max-evict 3`

iris: Customer-impact check: CS dashboard shows 2 customers with elevated error rates (cust-42, cust-99) — they are experiencing 5xxs on embeddings and generation. Marking P1-CustomerImpact: limited. @cs-pager can you notify account teams?

cs-pager: On it — sending a templated note to account owners for cust-42 and cust-99. (message sent) :email:

mikhail: Suggest applying temporary routing fallback to fallback-gpu pool to reduce new allocations hitting west2a. Proposed command: `redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --fallback-pool fallback-gpu --min-weight 0.2`

anya: Accepted. Applying fallback routing now.
```
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --fallback-pool fallback-gpu --min-weight 0.25
# response: routes updated, draining in-progress
```

sam: Drain started. Evicted 3 pods from gpu-west2a; autoscaler is spinning up replacements in fallback-gpu. Observability: p95 latency stabilizing, error rate decreasing but KV cache evictions remain high.

mikhail: Running quick health check on GPUs: `nvidia-smi` outputs show memory fragmentation + persisted allocations from stale processes. Suggest a rolling restart of the old runtime jobs to clear driver-held memory.

anya: Scheduling rolling restart for `runtime-infer` deployment with `maxUnavailable=1` to keep capacity. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-infer -n inference`

pagerduty-app: PD-8421 acknowledged by anya at 2026-03-17T18:06:10Z

anya: Restart kicked off. I'll monitor until error rate normalizes. If p95 > 1.5s after 10m we escalate to infra.

iris: Noted — CS will set expectation: degraded for ~10-30m for affected customers, mitigations in progress.

sam: After restarts, I see memory reclaim pattern improving. KV cache evictions drop from 18/min -> 6/min. Latency trending down.

anya: Good. PD note: mitigations applied (drain + fallback + rolling restart). Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Keeping PD open for 30m monitoring window.

mikhail: Filing an ops follow-up to investigate persistent fragmentation and whether we should add a periodic driver GC on restart. Creating ticket OP-3176.

cs-pager: Cust teams notified. Two customers acknowledged, will update if any escalation.

anya: Final check: p95 returned to baseline, error rate back to normal. I'll resolve PD if stable for the monitoring window. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-app: PD-8421 status -> resolved by anya at 2026-03-17T18:11:40Z (condition: stable 10m).

anya: Creating quick incident note for postmortem: cause = GPU memory fragmentation + aggressive prefetch pattern on kvcache; impact = brief customer errors on embeddings/generation; mitigation = drain + fallback routing + rolling restarts; action items = OP-3176 (driver GC), OPT-993 (rate-limit prefetch per-model). I'll put a short writeup in #incidents and link the ticket.

mikhail: ack — will add logs and `nvidia-smi` dump to OP-3176.

anya: closing thread.
